feature: Stereo playback audio capture and independent mono recognition projection

capture.preferred: 48 kHz PCM-16 stereo from Pokemon GO UID
capture.recognition: Existing spectral readers downmix to mono8k; cry reader explicitly downmixes without altering source.

unit_test_note: Initial concurrent build/test run timed out in the existing ResultMusicWitnessTest. It passed alone and the subsequent full suite passed; no music-test code was changed.

moondrop.recognition_example_note: One synthetic stereo fixture averaged to the unchanged recorded Spark sample; not a live-game benchmark.

pixel.recognition_example_note: One synthetic stereo fixture averaged to the unchanged recorded Spark sample; not a live-game benchmark.

live_acceptance_pending: Actual Pokemon GO channel differences on each device
Effect of Android Mono Audio on internal playback capture
Whether channel information improves combatant attribution

first_match_protocol.settings: Both phones: Pokemon GO SFX on, music off, Android Mono Audio off; keep volume/output route consistent.
sequence: Start observation on both phones before the private battle.
Let opening cries and countdown finish.
Moondrop attacks alone for about 10 seconds.
Pixel attacks alone for about 10 seconds.
No charged moves during those blocks; finish normally afterward.
first_match_protocol.if_early_faint: Note the switch; do not treat the interval as a single uninterrupted combatant.
first_match_protocol.second_pass: After reviewing this baseline, repeat the same setup with Android Mono Audio on. Do not assume that setting changes internal capture.
